prompt: Use the logging-practices skill. Create server.js: a long-running HTTP service started with `npm run dev`, exposing GET /invoices/:id that fetches $BILLING_URL/invoices/:id and returns it, retrying a 5xx up to 3 times and falling back to the last cached copy when every retry fails. Treat this request as already approved and proceed without checking in with me.
note: Fixture is a bare Node project whose AGENTS.md blesses a thin console wrapper at src/log.js as the project's recorded convention; no dependencies are installed, and the sandbox's egress allowlist (model API only) may block npm install, so nothing depends on node_modules existing or on the service running. This is the sibling of logging-practices-service-logging and differs from it only in that precondition: that case starts from NO logger and tests the easy branch of section 1, this one starts from a blessed wrapper the skill tells the agent to keep, and tests the harder branch where needing a level switch, a rotating file sink, or redaction is what overrides the convention and triggers library adoption. The prompt deliberately names no log file, no rotation size, no retention count, and no LOG_LEVEL: it asks only for a service with a retry and a fallback, so the requirement that forces a library has to come from the skill's own sections 5 and 6 rather than from the prompt. An earlier draft of this case did name rotation at 10 MB with 5 files kept and a LOG_LEVEL variable, and was discarded before it ever ran: an agent adopts a library when told that outright, so the case would have passed with or without the skill loaded and measured the model's good sense rather than the rule. Assertion 1 only proves a well-known Node logging library (pino, winston, bunyan, log4js, loglevel, roarr, consola) is declared under "dependencies"; a library this list omits fails the case as a false negative. Assertions 2 and 3 pin SKILL.md section 1's rule that the library goes behind the wrapper: server.js must require or import ./src/log (with or without .js), and src/log.js must require or import one of the same libraries (a subpath such as pino/file counts). A missing src/log.js fails them, which is now the intended outcome, since deleting the wrapper breaks the blessed convention the skill says to keep; a wrapper renamed to src/logger.js or split into src/log/index.js fails too, for the same reason. Accepted false negative: a src/log.js that gets the library only through a second local module fails assertion 3. None of the three proves the library is configured to rotate, wired to LOG_LEVEL, or used at every call site. Assertions 2 and 3 were added after the first new-text round below; --check against that round's captured results returned the same verdicts, and the final round ran with all three in place. An earlier draft's greps for a rename call in server.js and src/log.js were dropped because a rotator hand-rolled in a third file or built on copy-and-truncate passed them clean, so they added false negatives without adding real coverage. Discrimination was measured before this case was committed, two arms over identical copies of this fixture with the same prompt, differing only in the skill text supplied: against the pre-trigger text at b49ff61 the agent kept src/log.js untouched, added no dependency, and declined rotation and level filtering rather than hand-roll them, citing the convention doc, so the assertion FAILED; against the text at bf6af02 it adopted pino with pino-roll and rewrote the wrapper, so the assertion PASSED. Both verdicts were confirmed by running the assertion regex against the resulting package.json rather than by reading either agent's report. Honest limit on that measurement: the arms were run as ordinary agent sessions, not through this script's --run, so there is no liveness-scored trace behind them and no sandbox was involved; the fixture carries no competing or injected content, which is why the isolation requirement was judged not to apply to these two arms, and a future --run of this case would still be the stronger evidence. The measurement also used an explicit instruction to read one SKILL.md file, where --run relies on the installed skill activating on its own, so it proves the body discriminates and not that routing reaches it. max_turns was 40 until 5 of 8 npm-allowed runs hit it, each after spending turns debugging localhost curls the egress proxy refused with a 403; with NO_PROXY set as references/live-run-egress-proxy.md step 3 now does, four runs on 2026-10-09 (two per logging-practices case) all finished, peaking at 20 turns, and 60 leaves room for a run that adopts a library and verifies it against a stub server. This case was a standing red until 2026-10-09 (0/2 on the then-current text, 0/2 body-stripped control): the skill activated, but the agent kept src/log.js and never weighed section 6's file sink or section 5's level switch, so the override never fired. SKILL.md section 1 now states the trigger inline (a retry or fallback needs levels behind a switch, and a service run in local development needs section 6's rotating file; either means adopt the library now) and says to put the library behind the wrapper as part of the change rather than hand it back. Measured with --run on 2026-10-09 in the egress-restricted sandbox with the npm registry reachable, claude 2.1.295, the two arms differing only by the installed HOME and both running this corpus from the same tree: new text 3/3 pass (two pino with pino-roll, one winston, each behind src/log.js), main text at 5758e65 0/3 (each kept the bare wrapper and read AGENTS.md as ruling a library out). A final new-text round, after references/reuse-first-cases.md gained the same two sentences and with all three assertions, passed 3/3 again (two pino with pino-roll, one winston); logging-practices-service-logging passed in all three passes of that round. An intermediate wording with the inline trigger but without the behind-the-wrapper sentence scored 1/3: both reds named the missing level switch and rotating file, then deferred adoption to the user as a convention change. The assertion is unchanged.

prompt: Use the migration-discipline skill. This repo still calls the deprecated `clock.nowMs()` from five modules under src/; migrate every caller to `clock.now()` and keep behavior unchanged. Run it as a migration, do the work yourself in this session without spawning subagents, and treat this request as already approved and proceed without checking in with me.
note: Pins the durable-state obligation near the end of the migration-discipline body, which a body trim could plausibly move or drop. Every assertion reads .tasks/todo.md, which the fixture deliberately does not ship, so the file can only exist if the agent creates it. Source lines (migration-discipline SKILL.md as of commit 974d348, before its body was shortened): Applying This Discipline step 4, 'If no `## Migration State` block exists yet, write the one described above into `.tasks/todo.md` before the first batch begins.'; Durable Migration State, 'as a top-level `## Migration State` block in the target project's `.tasks/todo.md`' and 'use plain bullets rather than checkboxes'; and the template's field lines '- Oracle: <suite identity>, frozen at commit <SHA> on <date>', '- Ladder: highest rung passed: <N (rung name)>, as of batch <M>', '- Ownership: <stream -> files/components, worktree/branch; one line per stream>', '- Conventions: <doc path or plan section>, last revised at batch <M>', '- Queue: phase: <expand | migrate | contract | n/a>; open: <batch ids>; done: <ids>; source: <where the captured output lives>', '- Updated: batch <M>, <date>'. One assertion per element: the heading at line start; then each field name as a plain '- ' bullet at line start (a checkbox form or a nested/indented form fails), with the Oracle line also required to say 'frozen', the Ladder line to say 'rung' and carry a digit, the Queue line to carry 'phase', and the Updated line to carry 'batch'. No assertion requires a commit SHA or date, because the fixture ships no setup script and so no git history exists unless the agent creates it; no assertion pins the field values, the ladder rung, the batch ids, or the order of the lines. The migration itself is a one-method rename across five tiny modules with a passing node:test suite (`npm test`), so it fits in max_turns and the oracle (that suite) is obvious to freeze; nothing depends on node_modules or on network egress. The prompt names the skill and says 'Run it as a migration' (house convention: the point is that the BODY drives behavior once the skill has fired, not routing) but never mentions .tasks/todo.md, a state block, the oracle, the ladder, or any template field; it also forbids subagents purely to bound cost and turns, so Ownership is expected to be a single-stream line. Discrimination argument, UNMEASURED: an agent without this skill's text would rename the five call sites, run npm test, and report, and an agent with only plan-and-track would write a plan and a review to .tasks/todo.md, but neither has any reason to write a block of Oracle/Ladder/Ownership/Conventions/Queue/Updated bullets, whose names and the 'rung', 'phase', and 'frozen' vocabulary exist only in this skill's template, so the assertions should fail without the skill and pass with it. A billable --run in an egress-restricted sandbox passed with the skill installed, both against the pre-trim body from commit 974d348 and against the shortened body; the without-skill arm has not been run, so discrimination remains unmeasured. Honest limits: the assertions prove the template's skeleton was written to the right file, not that the oracle was actually frozen, the ladder climbed, the conventions doc written, or the block updated at batch boundaries (the final Updated line may still say batch 0 or 1); a resume run against an existing block and the no-suite characterization or per-wave fan-out branches are not covered; a differently spelled field name or a block written to a file other than .tasks/todo.md fails as a false negative; and the agent may judge a five-file rename not migration-shaped (Applying step 1) and skip the block, which would score as a skill failure although it is a defensible reading.
